name: portable-pi
description: Self-contained portable pie (pi-coding-agent) on a USB drive. Windows x64 + Linux x64. No host installation, no dependency on any other device on the network.

runtimePackages.name: @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
runtimePackages.reason: CLI + agent core, prebundled ESM (no runtime deps needed)

runtimePackages.name: @earendil-works/pi-tui
runtimePackages.reason: native prebuilds for win32/linux/darwin x x64/arm64 are resolved at runtime via require.resolve

runtimePackages.name: @silvia-odwyer/photon-node
runtimePackages.reason: WASM image resize/EXIF (dynamic import, optional but keeps image support)

optionalPackages.name: quickjs-wasi
optionalPackages.reason: codemode worker (WASM). Enable only if codemode is needed.

pi.launchArgsNote: -ns disables ALL discovered skills (including the host ~/.agents/skills) while explicit --skill paths keep loading. This is the isolation guarantee.

node.extractOnLinuxNote: npm/npx/corepack are symlinks in the tarball; exFAT has no symlinks, so build must dereference them (cp -rL) or write wrapper scripts.

minGit.reason: MinGit ships usr/bin/sh.exe which IS GNU bash 5.3 (cygwin build), plus the coreutils. Copying sh.exe to bash.exe satisfies pi's bash.exe lookup. 376 files / 93 MB extracted vs 9.622 files / 392 MB for PortableGit.

portableGitOptional.note: only if a host needs a fuller MSYS2 toolchain; not used by default

git.reason: pi's bash tool searches PATH and Program Files\Git for bash.exe. A virgin Windows host may have neither. This also provides git for worktrees/checkpoints. Linux hosts always have bash.

notOverridden.HOME: kept from host: git/npm user config still works; skills isolation is guaranteed by -ns instead
notOverridden.APPDATA: kept from host: pi does not use it once PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR is set; overriding it breaks Windows tooling

guarantees: <usb>/config/pi/sessions holds every session; the host ~/.pi/agent is never read or written
pi extensions, packages, MCP servers, prompt templates and themes come from <usb>/config/pi only

include.name: frontend-ui-engineering
include.reason: pure instructions; only optional npx tooling mentioned

include.name: impeccable
include.reason: ships a self-contained engine binary (win-x64); on other platforms it downloads once on first run. No local device needed.
include.caveat: Windows binary bundled; Linux/macOS engine fetched at first use (internet required)

exclude.name: contextvault
exclude.reason: needs the ContextVault Core DB + semantic embedding server on the Pi 5 (pi5=True, nitro). Network device.

exclude.name: voice-nitro
exclude.reason: needs the XTTS server on the Nitro (127.0.0.1:8123). Explicitly excluded by the owner.

exclude.name: voice-starlitram
exclude.reason: needs the TTS server on StarlitRAM (192.168.50.185:8008). Explicitly excluded by the owner.

exclude.name: voice-clone
exclude.reason: clones voices on StarlitRAM (:8008) and copies profiles to /mnt/d/audio-server on the Nitro. Network device.

exclude.name: vision-toolkit
exclude.reason: local CV models (SCUNet/YOLO/SAM2) installed on the Nitro GPU box.

exclude.name: graphify
exclude.reason: requires the graphify CLI plus redis (localhost:6379) and neo4j (localhost:7687) and a python/uv toolchain.

exclude.name: session-rotation
exclude.reason: requires pi-rotate (python) in D:\openclaw\bin plus a WSL shim in ~/.local/bin. Host-specific paths.

exclude.name: subagent
exclude.reason: requires the pi-toolkit extension to provide the subagent tool (phase 2 option).

exclude.name: pi-subagents
exclude.reason: requires the pi-subagents extension and spawning child pi processes (phase 2 option).

exclude.name: pi-intercom
exclude.reason: requires the pi-intercom extension and a second live pi session on the same machine.

exclude.name: playwright-browser
exclude.reason: requires @playwright/cli plus browser binaries (hundreds of MB, downloaded on demand).

exclude.name: llm-wiki
exclude.reason: requires the pi-llm-wiki extension and an existing vault (16 MB package + wiki state).

exclude.name: loop
exclude.reason: its workflow calls the subagent tool (7 references), which comes from the pi-toolkit/pi-subagents extension. Phase 2 with subagent.

phase2: pi-subagents extension (13 MB, pure JS) mounted on the drive: would enable subagent, pi-subagents, council-mode and loop skills
requires a pi shim on PATH so child processes can spawn, plus a child-spawn isolation test

auth.warning: auth.json contains OAuth tokens / API keys in plaintext. If the drive is lost, revoke them. Recipe documented in README.

settings.json.dropReason: packages reference host paths and would auto-install network packages at startup; llm-wiki.embeddingBaseUrl points at the Pi 5 (192.168.50.222:8093)

models.json.transform: keep providers only if baseUrl is a public endpoint; apiKey must stay an $ENV reference
models.json.note: current content is the cloud provider openmodel (apiKey $OPENMODEL_API_KEY) -> portable as-is

AGENTS.md.content: portable rewrite: no Telegram bridge, no D:\\openclaw paths, keeps the git push policy and the Italian default

env.content: optional API keys (OPENMODEL_API_KEY etc.), never committed
